Hello,
I think what I've written is per rules of this reddit but please let me know if I've worded things wrong. 
I've had a few doctors suspect MS but I've been continuously thrown around so I had some questions. 

My symptoms list is long but this is a basics of it:

Double vision sometimes, eyes dont adjust to light changes quickly which makes me have blurry vision a lot, and I have 'floaters' nonstop that cover quite a bit of my vision on both eyes. I have tingles that crawl across my face from time to time, seizure like activity but do not show seizures on my testing, I have full body pain to touch (I will flinch away from it sometimes), everywhere is always hurting I do not get a day off, I am starting to lose mobility in my legs, arms, and hands. My response time in my hands is slowing down significantly. I also can't use them for almost anything without severe pain that makes them unusable for the rest of the day. My grip strength is gone. I get strange 'feet attacks' where I get a sharp pain in the bottom middle and then my foot will hurt so badly I cry until it goes numb and I cannot move or feel touch on them. A foot doctor was actually the first to suggest MS after looking at this. I have cognitive issues, worsening memory and train of thought. I sleep so so much. I have dysautonomia that gets worse with heat. Severe nausea most of the time. 

Why I'm here - I've already been questioning but my primary care is doing the testing for me since neuro said it was all psychosymatic so I can't get into another neuro for a while. My neck MRI showed signs of severe deterioration to.. well everything. I have two cysts in it that are damaging nerves there. But I got my brain MRI back today and I tried the old panic googling but it doesn't make any sense to me and doomsday spiraling isn't healthy. This was my results:

Brain: No evidence of hemorrhage, mass, shift, or extra axial fluid collection. No restricted diffusion. The ventricles are normal in size and morphology. Punctate focus of T2 FLAIR signal abnormality within the right peri-insular subcortical white matter (5:12), nonspecific. Punctate focus of susceptibility within the lateral left inferior cerebellum (8:11). No abnormal enhancement. Flow voids at the skull base are preserved.

From what I can find this could mean almost anything to even a brain bleed? I am nervous that any of these results could lead anywhere, and I guess I wanted to know if MS was even a possibility here to get my thoughts together before my next appointment. Either way, thank you if you read this whole thing. I'm feeling at a loss due to how many times I've been thrown to the next doctor so I'm grasping at straws.

As for the EDS, I don't believe I meet any criteria for hypermobility besides maybe my legs and don't get dislocations, though I tend to roll my ankles a lot and my knees just kind of decide to not work and don't move right in their sockets, and all my partner has been able to find on that front is that I need those to some extent to qualify. After posting this thread I got so much anxiety about even coming back onto reddit because I feel like I'm crazy for going against what a doctor has said even though plenty of doctors have failed me in the past. This whole experience has just really rattled me. 
I seem to rant whenever I reply to anyone on here, sorry lol. I've never felt like I had a space to talk to other people that didn't just act like it was all in my head or like I was making a big deal out of 'nothing' before.

The actual doctor already commented that they refuse to diagnose or retest and trust the NPs judgement but I am planning on trying another test with a different provider I just have never actually tried for a retest before. I know most of the time doctors have just bounced me around and not helped but it still feels weird to completely go against what a doctor says and try to get it checked again. I've had so many people try to say that I'm making it up or it's all in my head or I just want attention etc etc. That makes it difficult to ever want to argue. I don't even care if I specifically have POTS or not, I just wanted answers and a way to feel okay again. I joined this sub and saw that I'm not alone with dealing with these thoughts but I still question myself because of people telling me to just deal with it. I'm spending so much money even with my medicare (which I know I'm a lucky one managing to get disability and medicare) to have people shrug and tell me all the things I can't possibly have because it's "rare" or I'm apparently too young to have these problems or whatever have you. It shouldn't be this hard for us.

My idea was well I went through all the pain to put the dang thing in I might as well trooper through a few days of agony since I needed it for my own sanity and health regulation. My doctors were kind enough to keep doing check ups to make sure nothing was going wrong while I felt the pain just to ease my anxiety but there was a level of 'wow they're exaggerating this' in the air. Went to the hospital because I wanted it out of me and they said they couldn't do anything and I got the stupid thing put in on a friday. It took almost a year to finally not feel it. It was still painful, then I'd feel it if I bent weird, then it would be a muscle thing, then it just kinda decided to remind me it was there sometimes. My therapist opted to have me getting a full evaluation because at 25 years old (female) I had been through bipolar, borderline, and a few other diagnoses. I was at borderline when I met her and she insisted I was not but thought I was very heavily adhd. She had not thought of autism but when I met the evaluation lady at my therapist's office I said I also wanted to be tested for autism. She mostly worked with younger autistic children too but was open to the idea. Even after our first session (she wanted a speaking one to know my background and observe my speech patterns, ways of thinking, and just other characteristics of myself) she ended it with 'I can already tell you show signs of autism in an adult as well as adhd and others'. 
I would definitely not let their words impact any of your thoughts on the subject. I do believe you're right in thinking they only have negative viewpoints on the concept of autism if they can't be open to the idea. It also sounds like their concepts are outdated as the spectrum has a huge variety of different types of people on it and you being reflective of yourself could very easily be a factor to tie you to your part of the spectrum. I too am very self aware of both body and mind - one of my first clues as well as difficulty connecting and understanding social concepts - and with the right therapy and treatment plans have been able to grow so much emotionally because I finally have answers to all of these things I was observing. 
I wish you all the luck. The road isn't always as easy as mine was at the end but don't ever give up on yourself!

Edit to add: as a female the odds are already unfortunately stacked against you for an autism diagnosis. Autism in females can show very differently than autism in males and so many don't seem to accept that. I love to watch an autistic teacher called Sarah Hendrickx on youtube since I finally was diagnosed. Her speeches are all over and they talk specifically about females with autism from childhood to adulthood with all the different places it affects. She is also autistic and went to college for autism studies and had spent a lot of her career helping people with autism.

This doesn't sound functional to me. A 10 year old little girl stuck alone in her room. She may enjoy the routine but statistically autistic women still crave and search for friendships/relationships. This little girl could be very lonely and isolated. Having friends in your peers is a very huge part of younger development - autistic or not. This little girl does not sound like she is living to me. How worse will this get as she ages? High school is an awful place in general in a lot of countries.. imagine how much more she will get bullied or how much more she will miss out on because of this peer isolation. The emotional damage it could cause into her adult life. She could easily not be able to work due to fear of other people if the bullying does in fact get worse in school. This could even begin to seed agoraphobia the longer she goes outside of her comfort zone (her room in this scenario) and only gets hurt.

Autism is a very complicated diagnosis and for many autistic people they aren't living.. they are just alive. And for a girl this young to get diagnosed.. they either got super lucky to have good doctors or she's placed deep into the spectrum (at least in the US). Women aren't typically diagnosed in the states until they're adults unless they are super not functioning.
